title: GOD'S PEOPLE NEED CHARITY, HEALING & TRUST

sense.text: “Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” Consider is the word. We don't consider the power we have with God. We don't consider the responsibility given to us, or the opportunity of repentance given to us.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.” From the top of this congregation, or any congregation or nation: if the head is not right, the rest of the body will fall apart.

Everybody comes in not really knowing what to do, so they look to the leadership to set the pace. A lot of times it is not even what you say, it is what you do in your life: how you operate, how you move. The leaders' job is to mold the people into better versions of themselves. But if the head is corrupt, the men behind him are going to follow, and the congregation hits a ceiling.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Sick from the head to the foot, and the wounds never healed.

The body of Christ cannot grow in unity while hatred, unresolved wounds, suspicion and selfishness remain among God's people. We come out of the world into this truth, and we all come in here sick, with issues we have to overcome. Growing a nation begins with the individual, the man or the woman, then the family, then the whole body together. As long as things stay unresolved and unchanged, you hit a ceiling.

precepts.why:
“For they were pricked, that they should remember thy words; and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulness, they might be continually mindful of thy goodness.” Situations will keep coming up to remind you to do right. These are fail-safes. If you are spiritual it is called a conscience: it is there so you don't forget, so that you consider.

This is for the leaders especially, and every man here is going to become a leader in his own right. If you are married you are already a bishop in your own household. You have to have a conscience toward God, toward what is right. When a man's wife says something that is scriptural, even without giving a scripture or precept, and he knows it to be right, a conscience toward God pricks him to change and do the right thing.

Isaiah's wounds were never “mollified with ointment.” Here is what heals: “For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.” The word is what restores us to health, our spiritual health, because we all come in here sick.

Leaders must acknowledge that sickness in themselves, see it in the body, and know that the way to fix the issues is the application of God's laws. IUIC is where it is by the grace of the Most High because the leadership pays attention and does not let anything fly, even among themselves: this is what the scripture says, are you going to abide in it? Then when they deal before the body they can stand with a clear conscience that they are not walking in hypocrisy. Even if the people don't know, God knows.

We have to be that example to the people coming in, to show them how situations are run and how you deal right with the people: honest, godly, and regardless of rank, God's word stands.

sense.text:
“Come, and let us return unto the Lord”. “For he hath torn, and he will heal us”: we were torn by captivity, by slavery, and he will heal us, meaning he will redeem us out of this situation. “He hath smitten, and he will bind us up.”

The prophets always spoke about impending danger, things happening in their own time and in the future, and in many cases they spoke of a redemption. That gives us a benchmark, something to look for in changing: the Lord will heal us, he will bind us back up.

“After two days will he revive us”: the two days are 2,000 years. “In the third day he will raise us up”: in the 1960s we began to learn who we are. The third day is the raising up of our people to who we are, to our identity, “and we shall live in his sight.”

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: then shall we experience this, if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do. Then shall we be bound up, then shall we be healed, if we follow on in the instruction God has left for us.

“He shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” In one word, a blessing. When we harvested crops we looked for the rain to come, and needed it. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us; that is how he punished us, as we read in Deuteronomy 28. The blessing the Lord will give us will be in the application of his laws.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince”. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

That's these days. We were out for a long time without the understanding of who we were as a people, or of what the will of God was for us. In the last days the Lord raised up the prophets back on the earth to teach the word of God and to apply it, so that we could be delivered out of here.

precepts.why:
Where does the New Testament say the children will return and seek the Lord? “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. That's us, reviving in this time. What we are part of and experiencing is the resurrection of Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign.

“For the Father seeketh such to worship him.” The Father is going to try us, to see if we will worship him according to the spirit and the truth. The truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Must: there is no other way to do it. Returning to seek the Lord in the latter days is worshipping him by the application of his laws.

sense.text:
“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” No truth: the application of God's law is not being applied. No mercy is being shown. No knowledge of God, because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. Our people have no knowledge of God, and it is our job to bring them back.

People are coming in because they buy into it. They believe they are the Israelites, and they believe what is being taught is true, so the word of God must be applied. One simple law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We cannot cook, clean, buy, sell or shop on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate: it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; nobody gets to decide it's not important. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. We can't reason it out in our minds; the Lord seeks such as will worship him as it is written, in spirit and in truth.

A man who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or congregates partially and then goes and congregates with somebody who has been put out of the body, is sinning: two cannot walk together unless they be agreed. People do that because we rationalize in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said no, my commandments are straight. Our thoughts are not his thoughts; it is a holy convocation, do what he said. It isn't hard. This one wearing a yarmulke, that one wearing this, that one going there: that is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the people's picture of what a godly Israelite looks like. They have to leave the right impression in the people's minds, based on the scriptures.

“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery”: all of it sinning. “They break out”: they break away from the law. “And blood toucheth blood”: violence, hatred, killing one another.

“Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish”. Therefore, because of what was read before. If the same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred and violence, the congregation won't grow or flourish. How is it going to grow if sin is prevalent in the body? The whole head is sick, the whole heart faint.

As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to the laws, and be an example of them ourselves, so people can see a change in the way we move and how we think. The truth is the only thing we have to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death. And what God asks of us is a small thing next to the sins we have committed. What's hard about not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath day holy? Minor things in the scope of eternal life.

precepts.why:
What is “they break out” talking about? “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave it, break away from it, shall die.

So Israel breaks out from the law by swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, and the end of breaking out is death. The end of keeping it is life.

sense.text: “A wise judge will instruct his people”: instruct them in the laws of God. “And the government of a prudent man is well ordered”: ordered as it is written.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: a wise judge of the people will make officers just like him. If you are a judge in here cursing people out and stealing, you are going to raise a flock of that. That is why some of these camps all act the same exact way, with the same mentality: they followed their leader. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is,” so are they that dwell in it.

“An unwise king destroyeth his people”: an unwise leader will destroy the people. “But through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.” The congregation is going to grow if it has a prudent leader, a leader who stands for the laws of God.

“Among brethren he that is chief is honorable”: the chief man, the Bishop over a place, is an honorable man. But look what follows: “so are they that fear the Lord in his eyes.” He has to see that these men are honorable too. That is called respect.

You lose the respect of the people when the laws of God are not being applied, when you deal rough and disrespectful, when you steal, when you lie. Then the congregation, the nation, won't grow.

“The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority”: you have to fear God to obtain authority so you can instruct the people. “But roughness and pride is the losing thereof”: roughness and pride in how you deal with the people, because those people you are dealing with are called of God. God called them.

“Great men, and judges, and potentates, shall be honoured”: potentates are leaders. “Yet is there none of them greater than he that feareth the Lord.” It doesn't say where he stands in the body. He could be the new man walking in the door, but if he has the fear of the Lord he is greater than those men, if those men don't fear God.

“Unto the servant that is wise shall they that are free do service”. As you grow in leadership you are serving the people, and fearing God is what makes us wise. The people serving him will freely serve him because of his wisdom. You want to be the kind of man people will do for because they respect you: not out of fear, not because you deal with them rough, but because they honor you. They see that you have a love for this truth and a love for God's people, and that you will go out of your way to bring about Christ's kingdom, and people will move for you. There is nothing the deacons, bishops and captains would ask of the men that they won't do or haven't done themselves.

“And he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed”: when he is corrected and has to change. No excuses; he accepts it and respects it. What leadership watches for is often not what you did wrong but how you handle it afterward. A brother can be all good, telling everybody else they don't believe the Bible, until correction comes; then he grudges when he is corrected.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites. “For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.”

“But all their works they do for to be seen of men”, and they love “the chief seats in the synagogues, And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.” They like the preeminence.

As another Bishop present recalled it: a revolutionary understands that 5% of his people will love him, 10% will hate him, and 85% don't give a f. It is so true. A brother once told a Bishop, I'll die for you, and he didn't even know the Bishop's children's names. It sounds good; nobody believes it.

We are all called of God, all God's servants, and the leaders see the men as godly men, important to this mission. However God worked out who sits in these seats, the leaders don't see themselves as more than the men. They know the structure and order of how things are done, but a good leader will never ask of a man anything that will bring dishonor upon him, cause him shame, or shame the ministry.

Twenty-some years ago a brother broke something he had bought, and a Bishop told him, just put it back in the box and take it back. The brother looked at him: so you're telling me to be dishonest? It was simple, but it was counsel to do something dishonest, and the Bishop had to catch himself: you're right. That is how you know we are moving different now. Come out of that old mentality.

precepts.why: “Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith”. The scribes and Pharisees were careful in the small things and left the weightier matters undone. That is what it is to “say, and do not”: commanding others while not doing it themselves.

“Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what thou speakest. Exalt not thyself, lest thou fall, and bring dishonour upon thy soul, and so God discover thy secrets, and cast thee down in the midst of the congregation, because thou camest not in truth to the fear of the Lord”. Thou camest not in truth: the Lord seeks such as worship him in spirit and in truth.

The hypocrite fakes it in the sight of men. He teaches the word of God but doesn't apply it. He makes merchandise of the people; he uses them and abuses them. After a while the Lord says, I'm going to pull your skirt up, embarrass you, and show you for who you really are.

And all along he was being pricked, but he wasn't changing; he got comfortable like that. We cannot build a nation, we cannot build Christ's kingdom back, with that mentality.

sense.text:
Still speaking of the wise judge: “Better is he that laboureth, and aboundeth in all things, than he that boasteth himself, and wanteth bread.” Better to work and build and abound in all things than to boast yourself as a leader and lack the things you need.

No man as a leader should be in a situation where the people are taking care of him. If a man doesn't work, he doesn't eat; by the sweat of the brow you shall eat bread. That's just what it is. You lose the trust of the people, and you lose their respect.

Imagine a nation of men who don't work, and their wives take care of them. There is a camp that does that. That's pimping. You goddamn pimp. How do you lie down at night with your wife taking care of you? Please go sleep in the kids' room. Imagine a camp full of unemployed men, the wife leaving $20 on the night table before she goes to work: don't go spend it all in one place. Shame.

precepts.why:
“Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us.”

“For we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you; Neither did we eat any man’s bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you: Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us.” That's the point. Not that the leaders don't have power, but they make themselves an example so you can see how they move: they work, they're not looking to the people.

As a leader, if you want the people's trust, if you want their respect, if you want to heal the nation, you have to work and hold a job. How can you instruct the people and show them how to build a nation if the head man himself and the men under him are unemployed, refusing to work and take care of themselves? “If any would not work, neither should he eat.” He must labor.

“For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.” They are commanded “that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread.” “And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed.” You are supposed to shame the man who refuses to work and fleeces the people: borrow here, borrow there, need this here, got this there.

Brothers do run on hard times, and very rarely will the body not help a man who holds a job, pays his bills, gives offerings and helps. That's not how we move. But it shouldn't be a side thing on the side. That is back in the world, and you lose the trust.
Paul asks prayer “that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith.” Not all men: some men are wicked and unreasonable men, and they do not have faith.

Brothers do fall on hard times: come to the leadership and they will help you. But when borrowing a little here and a little there becomes a pattern: “Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on.” That was going on here.

People are going to talk about you, because you don't have a job and you're always borrowing from this one and borrowing from that one: here a little, there a little, like precepts. Better is he that laboureth than he that boasteth himself and wanteth bread.

sense.text: “Who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us”. Whenever the offerings were brought to Jerusalem, Paul took with him somebody of good report in the body. He knew that man had no bad intent, but he knew how other people can be when it comes to money.

“Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us”. The abundance is the help given by the congregation. When the booster club funds are given to go out and preach the gospel, that is an abundance the people minister to the prophets, and the leadership has control of it. If the leadership dealt falsely with the money, buying Bentleys like the churches, the people would not trust them with it.

So among us the fail-safe is that the leaders don't touch the money. There are men over that, two people and backups upon backups, so that too much trust is never put in one single person and nobody can say it's on the leaders. There is a process the people can be confident in, so they know their funds are being stewarded the right way; not just anybody can touch those matters. When there is privacy around those things, it isn't to deceive anybody; everybody has different spirits. You avoid people even remotely thinking you are dealing unjustly, because we understand how people think.

“Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.” The Lord knows all things, but men have to be able to see it too. A leader should be in a place where no man can blame him. Otherwise it is a blight: people come in and say, this is like the church; that brother doesn't hold a job, so how is he paying his bills, with a new pair and a new phone? And the ministry gets blamed.

Trust between leadership and the congregation is built through righteous character, transparency, fairness, compassion, accountability and consistency. Across the line every school is supposed to follow the protocol and do things the same way: wash, rinse, repeat, cookie cutter. The systems are in place for a reason, and if you follow them you avoid this. The policies exist, but you have to seek them out; don't be so confident in something you haven't confirmed that you don't check with your leads.

“Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”. A leader does this with a ready mind, not asking how this can profit him or how he can make money from it. Feed them what? The word of God. Teach them the laws of God, apply the word of God, show them how to redeem themselves, and the people will gain trust. They will respect and trust you if your conversation is how to serve God and how to perfect your walk.

Not by constraint: not, well, Sabbath's over, I'm out of here, never speaking to anybody during the week. When the leaders get together they spend their time in the scriptures; they laugh and have a good time, but they are in the scriptures. Outside of this, what else do we have? If you've got another life outside this, you're not in the truth. If your best friend is somebody you went to school with, you're still in the world. There is no plan B. Prefer one another; if you can get together outside of work, spend time, because that is how you build relationships. It starts with the leadership: when the men see that the leaders are tight and go through the scriptures together, they will follow suit. If they see you cursing the people out and not working, they will learn the same behavior.

Peter had to write this because that was the mentality back then. Scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for reproof and for instruction in how to be righteous. It is left for us, so in the last days we read the same thing and know this is the blueprint we follow.

“Neither as being lords over God’s heritage, but being ensamples to the flock.” A lot of times brothers use their position and become lords over God's heritage. They take advantage because they have the rank, not understanding there is a God they are going to answer to.

We are to be examples to the people. Imagine the Most High sends Sacramento an influx of people, a thousand people repent, and from the top down there is corruption: a school ten times the size, with leadership cursing the people out, not working, taking money to pay their bills. That thing will fall apart. You want the trust of the people? Be transparent. Show a pattern of good.

“And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.” At the end of the day, we want this crown. The ranking system we have is for the running of the body, to keep things moving forward. The true crown is when Christ crowns you.

precepts.why:
Show a pattern of good: “In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.” Sincerity: not fake. You are sincere about this.

“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” Purloining means stealing. By not stealing you beautify this word, and people come and say, wow, we can trust them.

“Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.” Teach the young men behind you to be likewise sober minded: not purloining, showing a pattern of good works. The congregation must see the principles being taught demonstrated in the leaders' lives so the people can follow. The word of God must have free course in your life; when people see that, they will fall right in and do the same thing. It must be the word of God being taught and being applied, and that is how you gain the trust. You leaders who want the trust of the people: let your life be the example to them of how to move.

sense.text:
“Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.” Samuel gave an example: he allowed himself to be examined by the people. Whom did I take from, whom did I defraud? Show me, that I might restore it to them. That is a man you can follow and trust.

Transparency as a leader is golden. It is not a secret before everybody: show me where I'm in error with anybody. A leader does have the power to take advantage of people. It is ungodly, but he has it, and using it means you don't believe this truth, that this is about building Christ's kingdom back up.
“And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.” The people themselves bore witness for him.

precepts.why:
Things written aforetime were written for us to learn from: “He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” If you cover your sins, make excuses for them, or reason out why they are okay or acceptable, you will not be forgiven. If you confess your sins, are honest and come forth, the Lord will have mercy on you. Samuel said, if I did anything to anybody, show me so I can restore it. The man who hides behind his things and won't take accountability is the opposite.

What happened here in the past: a brother acknowledged what he did wrong. He said he did it, and he spoke to three or four of the leadership, captains there too. The Bishop told him that if he said anything other than what he had just admitted to, they were witnesses, and Satan had entered into his heart. The next day he said, I didn't do it. How could people follow that? Impossible. It destroys what is being built; it is moving as an antichrist, moving against God's kingdom and the building of it back.

The leadership principle: transparency does not require exposing every private matter, but it does require honesty concerning matters that affect the people. It has to be brought out; it cannot be brushed under the rug. A leader who wants the people to trust him has to be willing to listen to the people and hear matters out. When leadership doesn't move right away, don't think they aren't paying attention or won't do anything: there are systems in place that let things play themselves out. They are here because they care, and it is important to them to watch Sacramento grow and recover.

sense.text:
“Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; and the honourable delivered into other men’s hands.” But “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.” That is why leadership didn't move right away: they needed time to process what was going on and let it play itself out.

But it gets to a point where there is so much evidence that something is being done wrong. Brothers were spoken to a year before it all transpired and told it would be dealt with; they were being pricked. Then a trip was made across the country and brothers didn't show up. There is no way brothers travel to the other side of the country and the men don't show up. Once leaders get around the men and start talking, and things don't come out right, they dig until it makes sense. What they thought would happen was that it would brush by. That's not how it works; those are small signs, and it comes out in the wash.

“Answer not before thou hast heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk.” Sometimes you don't interrupt men in the midst of their talk, because they will put their foot in their mouth. They are their own worst enemy, thinking they are going to explain themselves out of the situation. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay.

A brother somewhere else was asked, did you steal? He said, no, I borrowed some money, but I put it back. Did you ask? No, but I put it back. If you went to the bank, took money without asking, and came back a week later to put it back, you'd still get arrested. You're a thief: you took without asking.

“Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.” Your lie affects the body. It affects the greater good of Israel. Put it away; we left the world for that.

Even if you're in error, admit to it, take the medicine and move on. You already did it; all you can do now is remedy it. Ask for forgiveness, fix the issue, and move on. But compound it with a lie, and now you're a thief and a liar. How are men going to trust you? How are people going to trust you if you lie?

precepts.why:
“Lying lips are abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly are his delight.” Deal truly, deal justly, be honest, even when you're in error, just be honest about it.

All manner of sin can be forgiven, but if you compound the sin with lies you just dig a deeper hole. You don't fear God. And then you want to sit and guide the people and show them how to serve God? People are not going to serve you, and they are not going to serve God correctly, with that mentality. And then you want to reclaim your place and sit up here as the example of how to serve God. No, it doesn't work like that.

sense.text:
Moses made wise men known among the tribes heads over the people, captains and officers, and charged the judges: “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.” “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”.

The whole point is not being partial: no respect of persons in judgment. It doesn't matter where they sit in the body. Right is right and wrong is wrong, and the laws of God must be applied. Set up as an officer, you have to judge righteous judgments.

And for the men who see and know something is wrong, it is their responsibility to speak up and say something. If they won't hear you, take it up. It shouldn't be one man alone, but the men who understand right from wrong and see that something is not according to the scripture. Even if you are rebuked by the very people you're speaking about, you have a God in heaven and you have a responsibility. If you know wrong and see wrong, say something and let the chips fall where they fall. If you have respect of persons, you're in the midst of sin.

precepts.why:
A lot of times brothers don't speak up because of what the Bishop calls friendship with a T. They let that govern them, and they are not dealing right. “But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.”

Respect of persons: this is my boy, so I'll slide him a little money on the side from the offerings, the congregation's money, the little benevolence pay on the side, because I know he's going through hard times. The scripture says the Lord identifies you as a transgressor. It becomes cliquish: certain people get special privileges, meaning sin-wise they get away with things, while you watch them judge other people harshly and this one gets a pass.

Favoritism destroys trust, because it teaches the people that relationships and rank matter more than being righteous, more than doing what God said to do. The Lord wants such as worship him in spirit and in truth, as it is written. These small principles decide how a leader is viewed, whether people respect what he says, buy in and say, you're worth following, because you are following what the scripture says.

There is nothing said here that the leaders don't apply themselves, and if they're not applying it, may God deal with them. It's not a game, not he likes me or I like him. You are reading this and doing that? Then you're in error with God. There is a way to fix it: get back in line with these scriptures, because we are going to stand before God and answer for what we do in his body.

sense.text:
“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” Ye which are spiritual: those keeping the commandments.

Why did Paul say it? Think about Paul's life. He persecuted the church; he was a murderer. Having repented, he could see where the brethren had fallen and restore them out of his own experience, because he knew what it was to be in that situation.

We all come in sick. Sometimes leaders, brothers and in some cases sisters expect of people what they themselves have not been able to do or have not done; they expect people to be them. That doesn't mean letting people run over you, or letting sin just go. But some brothers in positions are rough with the people and deal with them harshly, and they themselves are not right; in some cases they are stealing, and they show no consideration or mercy toward another brother. The roughness of brothers toward one another, and of some of the senior sisters toward one another: no.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.” Some brothers think themselves to be something because they have a rank. God said you ain't nothing.

As a leader you have to care for the people. Bear their burdens; be considerate of their plight, of what they are going through. Know how to talk. Some people you have to cut; some brothers are evil, and the scriptures say that some you save with fear and on some have compassion, as we know from Jude. But this is about brothers who are harsh, with roughness in their speech toward another brother. We came in sick. Imagine all the hang-ups we have that nobody knows about; if God decided to deal with us, none of us would make it. Care about the plight of your people. Some brothers sin and are really remorseful about it: restore them in the spirit of meekness.

precepts.why:
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.” Read before Galatians 6:1 to connect the dot: the brother who fell into sin, you meet him with the fruits of the Spirit, to restore his spirit and build him back.

Longsuffering is the one wanted here. Sometimes you have to be patient with brothers. The spirit of meekness in which the fallen man is restored is this fruit of the Spirit, and against such there is no law.

sense.text: “For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me.” The Lord is hurt for the hurt of his people. So how much more should we be? Are we not his people? Are we not in error? God is hurt to see us in this condition.

“Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?” Why? Because there is no leader to teach them and lead them to God. But God said the hour comes when the true worshippers will worship him in spirit and in truth: leaders will rise up in the last days and revive the people, leaders who care about the hurt of the people.

For the most part none of us are rich, and the little money we scrape together we have to be good stewards of. In other congregations the money comes in and they spend it in strip clubs; they spend it making action figures of themselves; they take the people's money and make it rain, while brothers give up the little bit they have and sisters send what they have, expecting the leaders to be right. It hurts to hear that brothers get help and still fleece the body and take advantage of it. Pray they repent, because they will answer to God for that.

Is there no physician who will recover the people, heal them, and show them how to serve God? This is the way to follow.

“Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father’s house have sinned.”

Nehemiah took responsibility and suffered what they suffered. He included himself. He wasn't just praying that the people sinned: I myself was in error, my whole house is in error. Consider that, as a leader.

“We have dealt very corruptly against thee, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses.” You want true healing of a nation? You want the people's honor and respect? Pray to the Most High and ask forgiveness for the people, and forgiveness for yourself, because you weren't right either. Consider thyself when you correct. This is the example Nehemiah left us: he prayed for the people and acknowledged himself.

As a leader, never separate yourself from the plight of the people. Never make yourself out to be above reproach, all-knowing and all right; nobody believes that. Find yourself in the scriptures and show that you are relatable to the people, that you don't stand aside from them. Healing begins when a leader stops distancing himself from the problems of the people and accepts responsibility for his part. We are all sick, all trying to get right, all making mistakes. Let the people see that in you.

precepts.why:
“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” That is what Nehemiah did: he prayed for the people, and confessed, that they might be healed.

Confession and prayer equal healing. There is no healing without confession and prayer. You can pray all you want, but if you don't acknowledge that you're in error you are not going to be healed. You'll stay in the same state, living a life of a lie.

sense.text: “Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?” The same thing read in First Peter: feed the flock.

“Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock.” They receive the benefits of being the head: they walk in and get to eat first. Should not the shepherds serve the people? The leaders are servants to the people.

Sitting here as leaders means nothing unless the people come to learn what is being taught; the strength is when the body moves collectively, and teachers are nothing without a congregation to teach. Their job is to serve: for those who seek learning, they are supposed to sacrifice their time and themselves to teach. It can't be for money, it can't be for opportunity, it can't be to get a bishop seat. If a brother's purpose is to lord over people, he has the wrong idea.

Christ gave his life to give us the opportunity of repentance, and he was without sin. For us, who have lived a life of sin against God, to come in here and lord over the people and take advantage of them: you might as well stay back in the world. It cannot be named among us.

“The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them.” You have not healed them, you have not taught them, you have not made them whole with God; with cruelty and force you have abused God's people.

It should not be named among us as leaders that we do not instruct the people, that the people take care of us and we deal with them unjustly and disrespectfully. There have been reports of brothers being cursed out, brothers threatening to beat other brothers up. In the truth? Fighting over what?
“And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd”. They have not learned, because there was no shepherd to instruct them.

“Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” “Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.” This is important: they love to learn and to apply God's laws. Don't spare the people.

“And the Lord shall guide thee continually”: guide those who take delight in approaching to God. “And satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

“And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.” That's what you want to be called: the restorer of paths to dwell in. You want to lead people back to the laws of God, to show mercy and kindness, and to show austereness concerning God's laws. There is no wiggle room, no play in God's laws.

Your example as a leader will carry on long after you are gone, because you set systems in place: you taught the laws God established, and that affects the generations to come. So as leaders, don't take it as a light thing; your actions have ripple effects. You restore the people back to God.

“Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain. And her prophets have daubed them with untempered morter, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them”.

Untempered mortar is soft mortar; it isn't strong, and it will fall. When you temper a piece of metal you heat it up, put it in water, bang it and heat it again, and that strengthens it. Untempered mortar is mortar that hasn't been strengthened, and it can't hold anything up. Her prophets have daubed the people with vanities, false things that can't hold any weight and won't survive the test of time.

“The people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery”. “And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.” The hedge is the laws that are supposed to guide them. He was looking for a man to stand up for the laws of God and guide the people, and he didn't find one.

We are supposed to be those men: the hedge to protect the people, to show them the right way and guide them down the path of what to do. A leader can't take on the title of leader and not be a protector to the people, a safeguard to them, the one they can trust to do the right thing. They come in not knowing better, and we are supposed to show them a better way to live, be the example so they can say, I want to mimic this.

So when destruction comes, they are tempered: the laws of God have been struck into them. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not covet. Like the package a Bishop said to return: now I learn, be different, be that example, so when the next person comes you can be that example to them. You are actively repairing the people, filling those breaches, instructing them in the laws of God: this is how you keep the Sabbath; brother, you've got to work, nobody can take care of you. You want the people to respect you? Be that example. Always speak from the place of healing the people.
This goes back to Galatians, restoring a brother in the spirit of meekness: “There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.”

“The lip of truth shall be established for ever”: for generations, as Isaiah 58 just said. The lip that teaches the law is established for generations, so when the next leaders come they will follow the same pattern. A big thing among leadership is succession. When the leaders get older and are no longer here, will the line of succession follow the blueprint of these scriptures that they enforce? The biggest thing is not to see the next line let this whole thing crumble and fall apart, and ask, what happened, did we not do our job? Imagine this legacy folding because the next generation is covetous, and nobody speaks up and nobody does anything.

“But a lying tongue is but for a moment.” It will fall apart. If leaders teach in deceit and hypocrisy, this whole thing will fall apart. But the lip that teaches the laws of God, enforces them and instructs the people will be the hedge to lead the people back on the right path, and it will continue for generations. This is about legacy: repairing the breach and reestablishing the nation of Israel.

This is what you're supposed to be: “I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called”. Vocation is purpose, and more: our job, our profession, our career, our occupation. We are supposed to be prisoners to this Bible, prisoners to the Lord's commandments given to us, and walk worthy of that calling. This is our lifestyle. It isn't something you put on today and take off tomorrow; you live this thing day in and day out. He isn't asking you, he's telling you to walk worthy of your calling.

What have we been called to do? To restore, renew, and bring our people back again to the heavenly Father. Our life career is to go out and teach this word, prophesy to the people, and build their spirit up, because it is in a low place, and only this word can build them back up. It is our job as men of the Lord to go out and feed them this.

Walking worthy of the vocation, we are to be servants to the people. The sacrifices leaders have to make are for the greater good of building back Christ's kingdom: time, money, and sometimes neglecting your own family for the greater good of the body. If this is about money or status, it will never grow. We can't come into this still lying and stealing; it doesn't work.

“With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” It's hard to keep the unity of the Spirit and the bond of peace if you're lying and stealing, if your conversation is corrupt, if you're f-bombing brothers. Not hard: impossible to grow. People are not going to buy into it.
“And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” In righteousness and true holiness: not fake.

“Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.” Corrupt communication comes out because men lie and steal. If a man does not work, he will steal; now he's got to pay his bills, and he will steal. Your lying affects the body, and your stealing affects the body.

“Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” You think it's just written there arbitrarily, right before let no corrupt communication come out of your mouth? You should not be stealing; labor.

“Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers”: that you can be the hedge to the hearers.

At the men's conferences, going through accountability and integrity and how to build, brothers were in there sending pictures to other brothers' wives. You don't believe, bro; you're just going through the motions. When a Bishop gets angry teaching at the men's conference, the anger comes from a place of: we need to be better, we can do better. What are we doing? We are going to destroy this for money we could go out and work for, because we just don't want to get up and go to work? What, we a hoe for money? All that the men have built over the years by the grace of the Most High, thrown away because of ego. Shame.
“And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.” At the end of it, you are grieving the Holy Spirit when you lie and steal from God's people.

“But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant”. This is Christ speaking: the chief man is supposed to become a servant. That is the vocation you are called to. A leader is called to be a servant to the people.

The leaders are nothing if they can't do their job, which is to instruct the people, and if they are not instructing them wisely and properly they are of no profit to God. They are servants to the people, not the people to them. We are to feed the flock, not have the flock feed us. Like the Bishop whose anger shows at the men's conference: he demands more because he wants us to level up and be better. We're not going to get out of here like this.

“Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.” That is the blueprint. To measure up to the full stature of Christ that you read of in Ephesians, you have to become a minister to the people, a ransom, and give your life for the people. Anything short of that is not fulfilling the duty you said you were called to in this truth. Leadership does not exist to build, guide, correct and serve God's people without sacrifice, without putting your life on the line.

There is nothing asked of the men that the leaders will not do or have not done. There is no corner they will send you to that they will not stand on, and no financial commitment they ask the people to help with that they will not make themselves; otherwise it's hypocrisy. None of the leaders go without jobs and sit back while the people keep sending offerings so they can fly around the world. Some camps over the years said they were going to take the money; yet you see schools being built all around the world. The money goes back into building, not lining pockets. Nobody is driving Bugattis. A man like that, you can follow.

The principle: authority without service produces fear. Authority combined with charity produces respect and trust. Some men want authority, but they come with fear tactics; that is old pimp foolishness.

“Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.” Some people are very good orators. They can speak, they have great retention of scripture, they can explain all mysteries; but if they don't have the spirit of charity, they are just making noise. “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.” Give all your goods to feed the poor and your body to be burned, “and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.”

To speak with the tongues of men is to edify and bring forth the people. A man can teach and speak with tongues and gather the people, and they come in believing; and then he has no charity.

“Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil”. If you have the spirit of charity, you are going to suffer long, be kind, not envy, not vaunt yourself. As read in Matthew, we are meant to be ministers to the people, not to be ministered to.

Charity “Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth”: it does not rejoice in sin. We rejoice in the application of God's laws. Leadership loves to come into a school and see it in order, the men in order and learning the scriptures. Sit down and ask a man who has been around nine years some questions, and he can't break down St. John 3:16 or Galatians 3? Then the leaders there are not doing their job; they are not preparing these men.
“Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.” That is what charity does.

“Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.” This is about the man. Whatever gift was given to him, the spirit of prophecy, tongues, knowledge, if he doesn't have charity he will fail. Say he used the gift of tongues in different countries to bring out the word, but he didn't deal right with the people: eventually the Lord will get him out of the way, and all the gifts he had are for nothing, because he didn't hold charity. The knowledge he was given is taken away from him, and he is out the door.

It is like Christ telling the Pharisees they should have done the one and not left the other undone: good in the other things, but failing in charity, which a leader obviously has to have. Regardless of his gifts, he becomes a hypocrite. The people gather in, but without charity you lack meekness, you're not longsuffering, you're not kind, and those things will run the people away. That is why Paul said to restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. You can teach all these scriptures and all these breakdowns with a photographic memory, but if you don't know how to deal right with the people, the people will not stay.

“For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.” You don't know as much as you think you know. God has given all of us a dispensation of this, and we have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this Bible we don't fully understand, not concerning salvation. It is to humble us: we are not as great as we think we are. And this is Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he didn't show many of the other apostles.
“But when that which is perfect is come”: Christ. “Then that which is in part shall be done away.”

“When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.” The childish things are the things just talked about. We put them away and are renewed in the mind.
“For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us.

“And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because that is what keeps the body growing. It keeps people coming in, because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself, how you speak.

precepts.why:
What is the glass? “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.”

“For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”: that's the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God, “and the image of his goodness.” This Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. But we see it through a glass darkly: we don't have all of it.

“Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”. That is what it means to see “through a glass, darkly”: we don't have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God, and we look into it with the understanding darkened, until then, face to face.

sense.text: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”. These are the fruits of the Spirit also.

“And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.” Charity is the bond that holds this whole thing together, because people come in here sick. They're not right. Show mercy to them, guide them, instruct them in the laws of God, consider thyself. Roughness is the losing of authority; disrespect.

That does not mean being weak, or not speaking sternly. Some people you have to deal with harshly because they are ignorant; some brothers you deal with harshly because they have been around too long to be doing certain things; some young brothers you kind of wink at. So don't go too far the other way. But above all these, put on charity, the bond of perfectness. Perfectness is to be complete and whole, that we all measure up to the full stature of Christ.

precepts.why: “Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous”. That is showing charity, the charity to be put on above all these things.

“And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.” Above all things, as Colossians says. Have fervent charity among yourselves: be longsuffering, be kind, don't vaunt yourself. You want your sins covered? Show charity. Be merciful. This is how you establish yourself, how you get the respect of the people, how you heal the body. If you want people to understand how to serve God, be the example; this is how people are going to know we are Christ's disciples, by how we deal.

As a leader you need to listen, acknowledge, confess, correct, learn to forgive, and restore. You have to rebuild the trust of the people, pray and intercede for the people, and demonstrate that your behavior has changed. Being a leader doesn't mean you will be perfect; you will make mistakes. The worst thing to do is compound a mistake with lies, take no accountability, and then expect the people to respect you and trust you. Be fervent in the laws of God, teaching them and enforcing them, but balance it with mercy, because we are not all right.

sense.text: “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.” We want to be known as the repairer of that breach. We have been in it for generations, and we are the generation that is back here. Our job is to repair the breach between us and God. So the laws of God must be taught, and we must learn to be compassionate.

“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” “The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” What kind of laborers is he looking to send into his harvest? Laborers moved with compassion, as he was: laborers who care about their people and want to fill that breach, because our people out there are sick.

The people are coming in, and the leaders must be the example to them. Love your people. Do right by them. Be that proper example, or else you will hit a ceiling, and Sacramento won't grow, this nation won't grow. If you want to be those men, you have to walk the walk and live it. Show what the power of God can do.
